entries.english: On 11 June 1261 at Prague, Bishop John of Prague confirms Wok von Rosenberg’s gift to the monastery of Hohenfurt of the right of patronage over the church of Wesely. Wok, marshal of Bohemia, had granted the right, which he lawfully and peacefully held, to his Cistercian foundation of Hohenfurt for its support, with the consent of his noble wife Hedwig. The bishop confirms the church’s patronage to the monastery in perpetual possession by his authority and forbids anyone to violate this confirmation, under penalty of excommunication. The two seals formerly attached to this charter are no longer extant. The entry also records a charter of 29 June 1261 at Richenowe: Agnes, widow of Pilgrim von Witlingau and dedicated to God, gives the church of German Reichenau near Gratzen to the monastery of Hohenfurt. She makes the donation for the remission of her husband Pilgrim’s sins and those of their ancestors, with the consent of her sons Wok and Zezimir, her kinsmen Wok the founder of Hohenfurt, Hoierius, and Bodivoi, and their other relatives. The witnesses include Abbot Otto, prior Adam, the priest and monk Otto, Gallus, parish priest of Predal, the knight Stlzlaus, and others. The act was done at Richenowe on the feast of Saints Peter and Paul in 1261. Agnes had the charter sealed with the seal of her deceased husband and that of his brother, lord Hoierius, who was still living.
